issues.description: Full-sentence audit (labels ignored) found no unambiguous grammatical error. The marked span B, "often leaves individuals feeling isolation," is standard written English: "feel" is lexically ambiguous between a linking verb taking a predicate adjective ("feel isolated") and a transitive verb taking an abstract-noun direct object ("feel isolation/fear/joy/despair"), and the latter pattern is common in edited prose (e.g. "left him feeling anger and betrayal"). No defensible reading of the sentence makes "feeling isolation" ungrammatical, so the intended error does not hold up, and no other genuine error exists elsewhere in the sentence either.

revision_requirements: Replace the verb "feel" with one that unambiguously requires an adjective complement and cannot take a bare abstract-noun direct object (e.g. "seem," "become," "grow"), or otherwise restructure the sentence so the noun-object reading is not grammatically available, before re-submitting this item under primary_target VERB_COMPLEMENTATION / tested_error_type incorrect_part_of_speech.

issues.description: "was the first researcher studying the mountain's seismic tremors continuously" admits a fully grammatical reduced-relative-clause reading ("...the first researcher [who was] studying X"), analogous to standard constructions like "she was the first woman running for that office." This is a genuinely competing parse to the intended "the first researcher to study X" (ordinal + infinitive-of-achievement) reading. The appositive "an effort that greatly improved eruption forecasting methods" and the ordinal "first" do bias a careful reader toward the intended infinitive reading, and this is a documented, legitimate ETS-style construction (ordinal/superlative + infinitive), so this falls short of an outright critical failure — but the alternate parse is real enough that the item should not pass without strengthening the context.

revision_requirements: Strengthen the sentence context so the reduced-participial reading of B is not grammatically available as an alternative to the intended infinitive-of-achievement reading — e.g. remove or rework the loosely-attached "an effort that..." appositive, or add explicit language that only makes sense under the achievement ("first ... to V") reading.

issues.description: The sentence's independent clause ("ethnomusicologists study traditional instruments") is itself perfectly well-formed; the actual grammatical problem is that the fronted correlative "Not only" requires subject-auxiliary inversion ("Not only DO ethnomusicologists study..."), which the shared taxonomy assigns to the INVERSION primary_target (explicitly defined as "subject-auxiliary inversion triggered by fronted negative adverbials" and exemplified in the taxonomy by exactly this class of fronted-negative trigger). CLAUSE_STRUCTURE is defined around independent-clause well-formedness/fragments/basic agreement, none of which is the actual test point here, so this is a clear taxonomy mismatch rather than a defensible approximation. The tested_error_type "missing_required_element" (missing auxiliary "do") remains defensible as the mechanism-level label even after the primary_target is corrected.

Recognizing the inversion requirement triggered by a fronted negative correlative is a moderately advanced point (and this construction was not observed at all in the 125-item Written Expression sample per spec §6.2); reviewer estimates MEDIUM rather than EASY.

revision_requirements: Recategorize primary_target from CLAUSE_STRUCTURE to INVERSION and update subtype to reflect subject-auxiliary inversion after a fronted negative correlative ("Not only"); tested_error_type may remain missing_required_element.
